question: Which of the following is NOT a dimension of the Human Development Index (HDI)?

options.text: The acquisition of education and knowledge
The standard of living and command over resources

solution:
The correct answer is __**Military strength and defence expenditure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite statistical measure used to rank countries based on human development levels. It considers three major dimensions: **Health, Education, and Standard of Living**.
 
• **A long and healthy life:** This dimension is measured using indicators such as **life expectancy at birth**. It highlights the overall health and longevity of the population. *Hence, this is part of HDI.*
 
• **The acquisition of education and knowledge:** This dimension is assessed by indicators like **mean years of schooling** and **expected years of schooling**, reflecting the educational achievements of the population. *Hence, this is part of HDI.*
 
• **The standard of living and command over resources:** This dimension is measured using **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**, which indicates the economic prosperity and living conditions of the people. *Hence, this is part of HDI.*
 
• **Military strength and defence expenditure** is not a dimension of HDI. HDI focuses on factors that directly contribute to human development and quality of life rather than a nation's military capabilities or defence spending. *Hence, this is NOT part of HDI.*
 
• HDI was introduced by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** in its **Human Development Report (HDR) in 1990**, aiming to shift focus from economic statistics to people-centric development metrics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dimensions of HDI:**

 
 
• **Health:** Measured by **life expectancy at birth**, indicating the ability to lead a long and healthy life.
 
• **Education:** Assessed through **mean years of schooling** (average education received by the population) and **expected years of schooling** (anticipated education for children entering school).
 
• **Standard of Living:** Measured by **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**, reflecting economic well-being and access to resources.
 
 
 
• **Calculation of HDI:**
 
 
• HDI is calculated using a geometric mean of normalized indices for each of the three dimensions: **Health, Education, and Standard of Living**.
 
• The **UNDP** publishes HDI rankings annually for countries worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Global HDI Rankings:**
 
 
• Countries with high HDI scores, such as **Norway, Switzerland, and Ireland**, typically have excellent healthcare systems, high educational attainment, and strong economies.
 
• Countries with lower HDI scores often face challenges in areas like health infrastructure, access to education, and poverty.
 
 
 
• **Other Indices Related to Development:**
 
 
• **Gender Inequality Index (GII):** Measures inequality in achievements between men and women in reproductive health, empowerment, and economic activity.
 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):** Assesses poverty beyond income-based measures, considering factors like health, education, and living standards.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Origin:** The HDI was developed by **Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq** and **Indian economist Amartya Sen** to emphasize people-centric development.
 
• **HDI Categories:** Countries are categorized into **Very High, High, Medium, and Low Human Development** based on their HDI scores.
 
• **Limitations:** HDI does not consider inequalities, gender disparities, or ecological sustainability, which are increasingly significant for evaluating development.
 
• **India’s HDI Rank:** As of the latest report, India ranks in the **medium human development category**, with significant improvements in life expectancy and education indicators.
